deductions: Clarity: “someone involved” is less specific than the stakeholder prompts in “Qualify and close.”
Actionability: “agree a specific next action” points to later guidance but gives no example in the 90-second brief.
Clarity: “Welcome channel partners as guests” leaves their place in the visitor-priority order unclear.
Actionability: “bring in the right M2M specialist” gives no handover cue; section 02 supplies one for product questions.
Tightness and organisation: “where a single network or coverage path leaves the visitor exposed” closely repeats the brief’s opener without adding a new prompt.
Continuity: “Use the lead-capture procedure” points forward without using the next section’s heading, “Lead scanning app.”
Clarity: “credible next action” leaves the qualification threshold to the rep’s interpretation.
Actionability: “flag other time-sensitive promises” does not say whether to flag them immediately or wait for the debrief.
Clarity: “contact route” in the failed-scan procedure could specify a usable phone number or email address.
Tightness and organisation: the “If a scan fails” paragraph combines lead recovery, app support and stand operations in one block.
Actionability: the failed-scan handoff says to give notes to Peter or Eerin that day but gives no next step if neither is reachable.

overall_findings: Section 04 does not meet the 95-per-dimension threshold because its failed-scan handoff lacks a fallback recipient or route.
No critical confidentiality or lead-save failure is apparent in sections 00–04. Section 05 was excluded from scoring and was not supplied, so its timetable and roster cannot be checked.
